text:
"What must be given should be given, but the final outcome depends on destiny." Hearing this, as soon as Somilaka woke up, he searched for the bag of gold. Seeing that it was empty, he thought: "Oh! How has the money I earned with such great hardship disappeared so easily? Since I am now a worthless pauper, how can I face my wife or my friends?" Having decided this, he went back to Vardhamanapura. There, within just one year, he earned five hundred pieces of gold again and set out for his home by a different path.

As the sun was setting, he arrived at that same Banyan tree. He thought: "Oh, what misery! What has fate decreed for me? That same demon in the form of a Banyan tree has been reached again." Thinking this and falling into a dream-like state, he saw those same two men on a branch of the tree. One of them said: "Creator! Why did you give five hundred gold pieces to this Somilaka? Do you not know that he is not entitled to anything more than food and clothing?" The other replied: "O Worker! I must certainly give to those who are industrious. The final outcome depends on destiny. So why do you reproach me?" Hearing this, as soon as Somilaka searched his bundle, he saw it was empty. Then, filled with extreme despair, he thought: "Oh! What is the use of my life without wealth? Therefore, I will hang myself from this Banyan tree and give up my life."

Having decided this, he made a rope of <term>darbha</term> <gloss>sacred kusha grass</gloss>, placed a noose around his neck, climbed a branch, and just as he was about to throw himself off, a man standing in the sky spoke these words: "O Somilaka! Do not commit such a rash act. I am the one who takes away your wealth, because you are not entitled to anything more than food and clothing."

<summary>Somilaka loses his hard-earned wealth a second time due to the decrees of fate and attempts to end his life, but is stopped by a divine voice. The story illustrates the concept that individual effort is governed by a destiny that determines how much one can actually possess.</summary>
<keywords>Somilaka, Panchatantra, Karma, Destiny, wealth, Banyan tree, Vardhamanapura, weaver</keywords>
